A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NRLB framework. Their complete main texts, appendices, tables, figures, and algorithm descriptions are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on four summarization datasets, agent and checklist ablations, and human comparisons with AgentSimp.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds direct-prompting comparisons, feedback-overlap measurements, efficiency results, and failure examples.

M1.justification: The agent pipeline, prompts, feedback prioritization, editing rules, and default refinement procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 clarifies the expert's summary input and removes unused reference-summary extraction, consistent with the procedure already documented in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate PLOS, GovReport, BillSum, and BigPatent with the same domain coverage and human participant groups. The senior-reader and learning-difficulty agent extensions already appear in v1. New analyses use retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C.4 and Table 9 add a direct, single-pass Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct baseline across all four datasets. This substantially broadens the comparison from AgentSimp variants to testing the value of the entire multi-agent procedure against direct prompting. Existing AgentSimp comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New evaluations compare direct prompting with one- and two-round NRLB and measure feedback overlap, latency, API calls, and cost. Existing dataset sampling, 200-example agent ablations, decoding settings, quality metrics, and human-evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds investigations of feedback redundancy and specialization (Appendix B.2), efficiency across refinement rounds (D.2), and precision loss and emerging context gaps (G). These extend the analysis beyond the retained ablations and successful case studies. The Editor ablation is relocated from v1 Appendix B.1, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Sampling seed 42, human inter-annotator agreement, and rating-dispersion reporting are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-model-run uncertainty estimates or significance tests; the added descriptive feedback percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All retained result tables preserve their numerical values, but Tables 7, 9, and 11 add substantial results. For example, direct prompting has PLOS ROUGE-1/LENS scores of 37.52/78.05 versus 41.64/66.68 for NRLB Round 2. Table 9 also reports BillSum Round-2 SummaC as 45.55, conflicting with the retained 34.55 elsewhere; this is not an established performance improvement.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. Existing readability definitions remain unchanged, and the pseudocode clarifications introduce no new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The third introductory contribution drops v1's broad claim of improved relevance over existing methods and focuses on readability and factuality through refinement. The central contribution remains the same unified framework for simulating diverse reader perspectives.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting feedback overlap to agent specialization, direct prompting's factuality to conservative information removal, and measured costs to practical applicability. Appendix G explains precision loss and emerging context gaps. Human-study generalizability is qualified more explicitly, while v1's JSON-parsing failure limitation is removed.

D1.justification: V2 documents the direct baseline's backbone and configuration, runtime/API-call profiles, and Round-3 costs. It removes the earlier disclosure of regex parsing fallbacks and skipped revisions. Existing full agent prompts and decoding hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Aher, Argyle, and Park et al. (2023) to support persona-based simulation. Section 2.2 explicitly acknowledges AgentSimp's iterative reconstruction and refines NRLB's distinction around accumulated feedback, replacing the earlier broader criticism.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methods, results, and appendix prose undergo extensive rewriting, including descriptions of unchanged scientific content. Terminology and headings are standardized, contributions are reformatted, and the Editor-ablation discussion and appendix organization are revised.

P2.justification: V2 adds three tables, revises Figure 2's arrows and spacing, and moves the Editor-ablation table into the main text. Algorithm typesetting, captions, and exhibit placement also change. Existing plots, prompt figures, and detailed case-study displays are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The added direct baseline, efficiency measurements, and failure examples make NRLB's tradeoffs easier to assess, while narrower claims and refined related-work positioning improve accuracy. The net gain is limited: new Table 9 introduces the BillSum SummaC inconsistency, the feedback-overlap interpretation overstates what three-way overlap establishes, and the earlier JSON-parsing limitation disappears.
